newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end much stronger, outperform U.S..
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end much stronger, outperform U.S..

text.p: Canadian bonds closed much stronger in active trade on Monday, outperforming U.S. issues, as the market's positive fundamentals attracted widespread buying in the wake of last week's selloff, dealers said.
"All the fundamentals are still in place in spite of all the volatility. It was a good buying opportunity," said Rich Wylie, a Toronto-based fixed income economist with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$1.20 to C$112.25 to yield 6.979 percent. The U.S. 30-year bonds rose 18/32 to yield 6.47 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 51 basis points from 57 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian bonds experienced their biggest one-day loss in more than two years on Thursday and weakened further on Friday before rallying to close slightly stronger. Analysts said the selloff was prompted by supply and technical factors and Canada's positive bond market fundamentals, such as low inflation, remain intact.
Analysts said that Friday's employment report for Canada, which included an unemployment rate of 10 percent, demonstrated that the country's output gap remains large.

"Taking a look at Canada, there's still so much slack in our labor markets we could easily withstand considerably more economic growth without inflationary fears here," said TD's Wylie. "The picture is still favorable from a bond front."
Dealers said today's buying was widespread, with interest coming from both domestic and foreign investors.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$1.02 to C$105.02 to yield 6.313 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.19 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 21 basis points at Friday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.81 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.98 percent.
